LESSON: RIGHTS OF NEIGHBOURS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.2: Rights of Neighbours
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rights of Neighbours, part of Muamalat (Social Relations) in Grade 5 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How should Muslims relate with neighbours? 2. What is the significance of upholding good neighbourliness?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search the rights of neighbours in Islam using digital devices/print media and make notes,

2. discuss the significance of treating neighbours well and display on a chart,

3. dramatise the right way of treating neighbours,

4. search for Hadith on the rights of neighbours and deduce lessons from it using digital devices/ books/resource persons. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search the rights of neighbours in Islam using digital devices/print media and make notes,
2. discuss the significance of treating neighbours well and display on a chart,
3. dramatise the right way of treating neighbours,
4. search for Hadith on the rights of neighbours and deduce lessons from it using digital devices/ books/resource persons. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rights of Neighbours together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skills of listening, speaking and teamwork enhanced as learners discuss the

significance of treating neighbours well and display on a chart.

• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners dramatise the right way of treating neighbours.

Values:
Love: caring for others as they dramatise the correct way of treating neighbours.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Interpersonal relations as they role-play/watch/ discuss, in groups, the rights of neighbours.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Social Studies as learners search for the rights of neighbours.
